The spellings Retthy Rete are important; it is clear that Reed was originally Reeth ; the spelling Rete being due to the frequent substitution by Norman scribes of t for th, especially at the end of a word. That Rete should represent the accented form of Reeth, and -rede (as in Cod-rede, Cottered) the unaccented form, is quite in accordance with phonetic principles. I have no hesitation, as already said under Cottbrbd, in equating Reeth to the A.S. wra^, * a wreath,' in the prov. E. sense of * enclosure.' The form Beed is not necessarily a corruption ; it would result, regularly, from the A.S. tor ad, a known by-form of lora^. See Cottered (p. 61).
